sources_considered.why: The October 2022 version directly evaluates recovery of implied meaning.
Contemporary primary evidence of improvements from instruction tuning, retained as a counterweight.
Much of the study measures data augmentation for separate intent classifiers. Its narrower classification experiments do not establish broad conversational reliability.
The evaluation concerns later models and a later period.

evidence_items.explanation: The study tests implied meaning rather than fluent text production and finds substantial shortcomings even in adapted models. It supports the ordinary reading that dependable contextual understanding remained a weakness, while acknowledging meaningful improvements.

evidence_items.locator: Section 1, main finding on labeler preferences
evidence_items.explanation: Instruction tuning had already improved performance on actual user prompts. This qualifies any reading that LLMs were useless for intent-related tasks, but relative improvement does not establish dependable general understanding.

unresolved_gaps: The cited studies do not measure reliability across the full distribution of household assistant requests.
The speaker supplies no numerical boundary for great or reliable.
